<USER_REQUEST>
# Phase 6 (Expanded): Reading Tracker with Full IELTS Practice

This replaces the original brief's basic Reading Tracker description with an expanded version. Everything else in the project brief and prior phases stays the same.

## Why This Changed
Personal goal: use reading practice not just to log articles, but to actively train IELTS Reading skills — comprehension under time pressure, vocabulary acquisition, and writing practice via summaries.

## Content Source (Important — No AI Generation)
Per the project brief, no AI-generated content. Articles and their comprehension questions will be manually copied in by me from free graded-reading sources like Breaking News English, BBC Learning English, or VOA Learning English — many of which already include ready-made comprehension questions I can transcribe. The app does not need to fetch or generate these automatically.

## Database Schema

### `reading_articles`
- `title` (string)
- `level` (enum or string: Beginner / Intermediate / Advanced, or CEFR A2–C1)
- `target_band` (nullable float, e.g. 6.5 — my self-assessed IELTS band target for this article's difficulty)
- `full_text` (long text — the article content)
- `source_url` (nullable string)
- `recommended_time_minutes` (integer, default e.g. 15 — suggested reading+quiz time, IELTS-style)
- `created_at`

### `reading_questions`
- `reading_article_id` (foreign key)
- `question_text` (text)
- `question_type` (enum: `true_false_not_given`, `multiple_choice`, `short_answer`)
- `option_a`, `option_b`, `option_c`, `option_d` (nullable — only used for multiple_choice)
- `correct_answer` (string)
- `explanation` (nullable text)

### `reading_attempts`
- `reading_article_id` (foreign key)
- `score` (integer — number correct)
- `total_questions` (integer)
- `time_taken_seconds` (integer)
- `words_per_minute` (computed: word count of article ÷ time taken, useful for tracking reading speed over time)
- `completed_at`

### `reading_summaries`
- `reading_article_id` (foreign key)
- `summary_text` (text)
- `word_count` (integer, auto-calculated)
- `created_at`

Vocabulary extracted from an article should link into the existing `vocabulary` table (add a nullable `source_reading_article_id` column to that table so words can trace back to the article they came from).

## Features / Flow

### 1. Add Article (Livewire form)
- Fields: title, level, target band, full text, source URL (optional), recommended time
- After saving, redirect to "Add Questions" for that article

### 2. Add Questions (Livewire form)
- Repeatable form to add multiple questions per article
- Question type selector (True/False/Not Given, Multiple Choice, Short Answer)
- Conditional fields: options A–D only show for Multiple Choice

### 3. Timed Reading Mode
- When I open an article to practice, show a start button
- Once started: display the article text, running timer visible (counting up, not down — I want to see how long I actually take, not be rushed by a shrinking clock)
- "I've finished reading" button moves me to the quiz; timer keeps running until quiz is submitted
- On submission: calculate total time taken, score, and words-per-minute

### 4. Quiz Taking
- Present questions one at a time or all on one page (all-on-one-page is simpler, prefer that)
- Multiple choice: radio buttons
- True/False/Not Given: three-way toggle
- Short answer: text input, compared case-insensitively to correct_answer
- On submit: show score immediately, plus explanations for any wrong answers

### 5. Summary Writing
- After the quiz, a textarea to write a summary of the article (this doubles as informal IELTS Writing Task 2 practice)
- Auto-calculate word count on save

### 6. Vocabulary Extraction
- On the article page (after completing it), a quick-add mini-form to pull out any new words into the main `vocabulary` table, pre-tagged with this article as the source

### 7. Reading Stats / History
- List of all past attempts per article (in case I redo one later) and across all articles
- Simple trend view: average score over time, average words-per-minute over time, band levels attempted vs target
- This feeds into the existing Stats & Goals module from Phase 8 — no need to duplicate, just make sure `reading_attempts` data is queryable from there

## Explicitly Out of Scope (still, even with this expansion)
- No auto-fetching of articles from the internet — I paste them in manually
- No AI-generated questions or scoring feedback — questions are pre-written when I add the article
- No official IELTS band-score algorithm — `target_band` and score trends are just for my own tracking, not a certified estimate
</USER_REQUEST>
